classification.difficultyReason: The named parts scaffold intercept calculations, equating two supplied line equations, and using two coordinates to find a gradient and equation. Exact surd arithmetic adds manipulation but requires no substantial reframing.

content.prompt:
A surveyor has drawn lines on a map to represent straight roads between towns positioned at $O$, $A$, $P$, $Q$, $T$ and $R$, as shown. Cartesian axes have been drawn so that equations can be assigned to roads. Distances are measured in kilometres.

The road through towns $O$ and $A$ has equation $y=\sqrt{2}x$, while the road through towns $P$ and $Q$ has equation $y=\sqrt{2}x-20$. The road through towns $A$, $Q$ and $R$ has equation $y=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}x+25$. The direction of due north is shown on the diagram.

Express all answers in parts a to d as exact values in surd form.

spec.description: Equation-driven road map with parallel rising roads, a shared falling road, town labels and a separate north arrow. O is retained because it identifies a named town.
spec.mathematics: OA: y=sqrt(2)x; PQ: y=sqrt(2)x-20; AQR: y=-x/sqrt(2)+25. P and T are intercepts of PQ; R is the x-intercept of AQR.
spec.answerVisibility: Town names and roads are supplied; numerical coordinates and derived answers are hidden.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the distance from town $O$ to town $P$ ($OP$).

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of town $Q$ at the intersection of the road from $A$ to $R$ with the road from $P$ to $Q$.

answer.short:
$(15\sqrt{2},10)$

Equate the two road equations to find their intersection.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{2}x-20&=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}+25\\2x-20\sqrt{2}&=-x+25\sqrt{2}\\3x&=45\sqrt{2}\\x&=15\sqrt{2}.\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $y=\sqrt{2}x-20$:

$$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{2}(15\sqrt{2})-20\\y&=30-20\\y&=10.\end{align*}$$

The other road gives $y=-\frac{(15\sqrt{2})}{\sqrt{2}}+25=10$, confirming $Q=(15\sqrt{2},10)$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: A new road is to be built through towns positioned at $P$ and $R$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Find the gradient of the line from $P$ to $R$.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Find the equation of the line that runs through $P$ and $R$.

answer.worked:
Using $P=(0,-20)$ and $m=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{5}$ in point–gradient form:

$$\begin{align*}y-(-20)&=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{5}(x-0)\\y+20&=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{5}x\\y&=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{5}x-20.\end{align*}$$

At $R$, the right-hand side is $\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{5}(25\sqrt{2})-20=0$, as required.
